dedupe_keys.name: a global high shift cycling scenario itdp and uc davis 2015

description: A Global High Shift Cycling Scenario is a 2015 report by Jacob Mason, Lew Fulton and Zane McDonald for the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy (ITDP) and the University of California, Davis, on the potential for dramatically increasing bicycle and e-bike use in cities around the world, with estimated energy, carbon dioxide and cost impacts. Coverage: urban passenger transport worldwide by region, with a business-as-usual scenario and a high shift scenario to 2050. The authors collected data on global cycling and electric bicycle ridership, found higher levels than previously reported, estimated recent cycling trends by region, and recalculated the effect of high bicycle use on energy use and CO2. A dramatic increase in cycling could save society US$24 trillion cumulatively between 2015 and 2050 and cut CO2 emissions from urban passenger transport by nearly 11 percent in 2050. Format and access: a report PDF, indexed in TRID and held in the University of California repository. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: the scenario dates from 2015 and has not been updated there; regional totals are not city-level data. The regional mode shares can be used as scenario inputs when simulating long-term demand and emissions of urban transport networks. It relates to the WHO HEAT tool and the BTS bikeshare and e-scooter systems data in the catalogue.
